chapter: Merv Griffin show and duo years
title: Bass and guitar duos: Ron Carter and Don Thompson
summary: The Playboy Club recording and hearing the bass as an extension of the guitar.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well, let’s go back and finish the bass/guitar story.
Oh, yeah.
Which is Ron, the Guitar Club on Tenth Avenue, I think it was.
Yeah.
And then, you guys did a gig at the Playboy Club that was a live recording.
Oh, yeah, right.
That was the first of the three duo albums.

Yeah. It reminds me I have to get back to that guy who asked about that record, I guess. Yeah, we, we played quite a bit together as a duo and still do sometimes. Yeah, that was recorded that way. It’s the only time I’ve been in a Playboy Club. (laughs)
Is there something… I don’t know if gratifying is really the word I want…
How are you staying so alert? This is disgusting. (laughs)
(laughs) Well…
You kids today…
Is there something… maybe challenging is a better word. Something that can pique your interest…
At the Playboy Club? (laughs)
No. In playing just guitar and bass?
Yeah.
The thing that makes life, musical life different from other things.

Yeah. Well, I hear the bass fiddle as a, as a lower extension of the guitar, actually, so that’s kind of how I deal with it. So what I do, I realize now, is I’ll… if we’re playing a standard tune, I’ll keep my ears on what Ron is gonna do with the bass line, and even if I’m playing… either playing a solo or just chords, I’ll listen to where Ron’s going. So I stay out of his register and… although it would be an octave higher, but it still could mess up the sound, and sometimes he’ll play something funny and I’ll catch it and we’ll kinda grin at each other, you know. So it’s like two parts of the same instrument, really. And I had played the string bass a bit in high school and music school, ‘cause we always needed a bass in the orchestra. I never practiced ‘cause I figured I’d ruin my hand for guitar playing but… I’ve always been really tuned into the

bass fiddle. That’s… Don Thompson and I had bit of difficulty that way, ‘cause when Don plays a solo, it’s marvelous, incredible music. His, all his solos he plays, it’s called thumb position. They’re always really up high, and it’s hard to accompany him ‘cause I’m bumping into him. We’re in the same register.
Oh.
So Don and I talked about that, too, and worked it out somehow. Yeah, Ron, Ron is just marvelous to play with that way. We listen to one another and crack up occasionally.
